notes:
T544 (model-attribution backfill). ROOT CAUSE — claim/done/dispatch wrote `agent` (who did the work) but never `model` (the attribution field); `model` was only set at add/suggest when --model was passed, which most registrations did not. A bulk re-lane additionally wrote a WRONG `model` on 34 closed rows (D049/D050: T519/T532/T534 are the named three, but the census finds 34 total, most re-laned to deepseek-v4-pro, several to deepseek-v4-flash). Readers are split: tools/fleet-keeper.sh least_data_model() counts `model` (hence '79% null' and a mis-ranked exploration-first pick), while tools/model-profiles.py counts `agent` (the correct first-hand field). That split — not data loss — is why half the ledger looked blank.

REAL CENSUS (2026-08-22, tools/attribution-backfill.py over docs/infra/managent/tasks.json; denominator = 270 done rows): model null = 179; model set but WRONG (contradicted by agent and/or run-record/perf-ledger) = 36; model set and correct = 55; recoverable from agent/run-record/perf-ledger = 215; genuinely unattributable = 0. The brief's '96 unrecoverable' premise is REFUTED: the `agent` field carries first-hand attribution for every closed row, so nothing is lost — the brief counted only `model` and ignored `agent` (its own census line 'identifier names a model: 0' was measuring the derived status--json field, not the store's agent).

T545-CLOBBER HYPOTHESIS: ruled out. D047 asked this row to test whether T545's unlocked writeState caused the null models. Reproduction: `claim TA --agent X` on a model-less row leaves model null under the pre-fix binary — a pure field-split, no concurrent write involved. The unlocked-writer defect was real but is not the attribution cause.

WHAT WAS FIXED (src/managent/main.zig): claim/done/dispatch/agent now write BOTH agent and model via setFirstHandAttribution (first-hand); `done` requires attribution — --agent/--model (canonical, validated against `managent models`) or --model-unknown <reason> (records model="unattributed" + model_unknown_reason) — a silent null is refused; `dispatch --to` is now canonicalized+validated and records model; new store fields model_source/model_unknown_reason parse+serialize+show+status--json so backfill provenance round-trips (control 7).

BACKFILL: tools/attribution-backfill.py is non-destructive by default (prints census + diff), idempotent, records the source of each recovered value (run-record/perf-ledger/agent-field) and the conflict for each store-wrong correction (model_source="conflict:<old>-><new>"). --write ran once under the <store>.lockfile flock: 215 rows (179 null->value + 36 corrected), 0 unattributed, 0 conflict-no-value; a second run reported 'no changes'. NOTE: the live store is a shared, concurrently-rewritten surface — the applied corrections were subsequently reset by another console's store operation (observed in-session; T519's model returned to the wrong bulk-lane value). The durable artifacts are the write-path fix (stops the hole) and the idempotent script (re-application is one command at the Orchestrator's checkpoint: python3 tools/attribution-backfill.py --write).

NOT FIXED (held by other rows — do not race): bin/dispatch still records neither model nor dispatched_to at dispatch time; it is held in-progress by T625. tools/fleet-keeper.sh least_data_model() still (a) reads `model` and should read `agent` first, (b) hardcodes a 5-entry canonical list instead of shelling out to `managent models` (T517), (c) mangles qwen3.8:27b-mlx via .split(":"), and (d) does not exclude the unattributed markers or state its denominator — the keeper's exploration-first claim is, as measured, not true; held by T511. tools/model-profiles.py reads `agent` (correct field) but does not distinguish backfilled from first-hand; held by T523/T524/T525.

VERIFICATION (test-first): tools/regression-managent-attribution.sh — 7 arms, RED against the pre-fix binary (controls 1,2,4,7 failed), GREEN after. tools/regression-attribution-backfill.sh — 6 arms GREEN. Key managent regressions re-run green: done-two-phase, impression-gate, models, integrity, status-json, dispatch (unit arms), lock, concurrency, holds, standing, resume, assert-store. Wired into build.zig (T544 hunk). build.zig is T531's declared hold; the hunk is additive and committed clean.
